items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Sponsored by the New Jersey Jazz Society in connection with -- or I should say the New Jersey Jazz Society working hand in hand with George Wein.

ctx.x: He continued his studies on drums, and along the way, after he went with Louis Armstrong -- he went all over the world with Louie Armstrong, and was such an outstanding soloist, and to this day, he's such a beautiful man, and he's still in the picture, I don't dare estimate what his age is -- I know it's around 70, and he's all over the world with Cootie Williams' orchestra, a small group, and they cover concerts all over the world, and they do some of the nicest work, and Cozy is still in there pitching. He is…

I must mention -- I did the first year of the Newport Festivals were starting, with Eddie Condon, for George Wein, Schroeder he was the promoter. We had Peanuts Hucko, Jack Lesberg, Gene Shrader, and Cutty Cutshall among others. And it rained

and it poured, and this great outdoor auditorium, and if you know anything about Eddie Condon, instead of playing the guitar, he took it upon himself to conduct the six pieces, and because of the rain which didn't cover the back, or the front of the show, where he announced, he had an umbrella over his head -- and it made quite a picture.
